minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed a skate park design, a Marshall Park grant application, and an extra beach lifeguard hire.
minutes.summary: The commission heard director updates on the beach and recreation programs, then reviewed the Marshall Park skate park design with its engineer. It gave feedback on the schematic design for Marshall Park, reviewed the state grant application ahead of its filing deadline, and planned outreach to the select board. Three roll-call motions were taken, and the captions give no tally for any of them.

votes.motion: Recommend adding an additional part-time as-needed lifeguard by name, with authority to hire someone else if his licensing does not come through, without returning to the commission.
Accept the skate park design as presented this evening.
Support the Park Grant application as discussed this evening.
Adjourn (first motion was withdrawn because the next meeting date had not been set).
Adjourn at 8:58 after setting the next meeting date.

budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed paying the vendor for a full minimum class even though few children enrolled. The cost was said to be small, drawn from set-aside money and program profit.
Prices and the vendor's cut were discussed, along with a markup that covers administrative and credit card processing costs.
Revenue from memberships and programs, including day passes, was reported so far. The board asked for a full breakdown of program costs and revenue at the August meeting.
Grant eligibility rests on parking capacity, and fees charged for the facility were attached.
A board member checked the percentages in the budget list against the line amounts. The author said rounding explained the differences and that the final budget now uses exact numbers.
figures_as_heard: 5 million one hundred thirty one five and eighty four

budget_items.topic: Community funding for the Marshall Park engineering
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair wants to thank the select board for funding the engineering work and the ARPA money. She also wants a letter from the board of health committing funds for the septic repair.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and four thousand dollars

decisions.decision: The commission agreed to let staff replace the named lifeguard with another hire if his licensing does not arrive in time, and the chair would email the town manager about it.

Staff would ask the vendor to run the multi-sports camp with seven children, with the town paying as if the minimum class were enrolled. Registration stays open and Angela would confirm with the vendor first.
Angela will draft a plan for a combined beach house dedication and cardboard boat race event, to be shared with the commission.
The chair will turn the facilities director's schematic design comments into a commentary and send them to the design consultant. The parking-space item would be struck.
The grant application would be submitted after final edits, with the lead applicant submitting by the deadline and sharing the folder afterward. The next meeting was set for 16 August.
The chair will seek a letter from the board of health on the septic funds and plans to update the select board under Communications from other boards, possibly the following week.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission took a roll-call motion to recommend an extra part-time lifeguard, with staff free to substitute another hire if licensing fails; the captions give no tally.
The commission reviewed the Marshall Park skate park design with its engineer and took a roll-call motion to accept it; the captions give no tally.
The chair will turn the facilities director's schematic design comments into a commentary for the design consultant, and the parking-space item would be struck.
A roll-call motion to support the state park grant application was taken, with submission after final edits and no tally in the captions.
The chair will seek a board of health letter on septic funds and plans to update the select board, possibly the following week.

why_it_matters: The Marshall Park design and its state grant application decide whether the skate park project can move to funding, and the select board and board of health may be asked to commit money for engineering and septic repair.

Beach lifeguard staffing and camp enrollment shortfalls are paid from set-aside money and program profit, so the August cost and revenue breakdown will show how much those programs rely on town funds.
watch_next: Next Parks Commission meeting on 16 August, with a full breakdown of beach program costs and revenue requested.
The grant application submission by its deadline, and the board of health letter on septic funds.
